chunks: And Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Aban ibn Uthman from Al-Hasan al-Tassar who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the temporary marriage (mut'ah) of the private part. He said, 'There is no harm in it.' I said, 'And if a child is born from it?' He said, 'It belongs to the owner of the girl, unless he stipulates otherwise for him.'

key_terms.صَاحِبِ الْجَارِيَةِ: The owner of the girl (referring to the husband in the temporary marriage)
key_terms.عَارِيَّةِ الْفَرْجِ: Temporary marriage (Mut'ah), literally 'borrowing of the private part'
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm in it (permissible)
key_terms.يَشْتَرِطَ: To stipulate (a condition in the contract)

ai.seo_question: Who owns the child born from temporary marriage in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of al-Hasan al-Taqqar to Imam al-Sadiq (AS), clarifies that offspring from temporary marriage (mut'ah) are legitimate and their lineage is attributed to the woman's owner, reflecting the principle that 'the child belongs to the bed.' The Imam’s addition that the man may stipulate otherwise highlights the contractual flexibility inherent in mut'ah, allowing parties to negotiate custody or financial responsibilities beyond the default ruling. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for determining nasab (lineage) and nafkah (maintenance) in temporary unions.
